cases.sentence: Сергей Иванович был в самом ___ духа и забавлялся оригинальностью Катавасова.
cases.explain: «хорошем расположении» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: On the day of the wedding, according to the Russian custom (the princess and Darya Alexandrovna insisted on strictly keeping all the customs), Levin did not see his betrothed, and dined at his hotel with three bachelor friends, casually brought together at his rooms. These were Sergey Ivanovitch, Katavasov, a university friend, now professor of natural science, whom Levin had met in the street and insisted on taking home with him, and Tchirikov, his best man, a Moscow conciliation-board judge, Levin’s companion in his bear-hunts. The dinner was a very merry one: Sergey Ivanovitch was in his happiest mood, and was much amused by Katavasov’s originality. Katavasov, feeling his originality was appreciated and understood, made the most of it. Tchirikov always gave a lively and good-humored support to conversation of any sort.

cases.sentence: – Более ___ женитьбы, как вы, я не видал, – сказал Сергей Иванович.
cases.explain: «решительного врага» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “A more determined enemy of matrimony than you I never saw,” said Sergey Ivanovitch.

cases.sentence: – А признайтесь, есть это чувство, как у ___, что в окошко хочется выпрыгнуть?
cases.explain: «гоголевского жениха» — after the preposition «у», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “And confess there is a feeling that you want to jump out of the window, like Gogol’s bridegroom?”

cases.sentence: Все лучше, чем ___, позор, неверность!!» С отчаянием в сердце и со злобой на всех людей, на себя, на нее он вышел из гостиницы и поехал к ней.
cases.explain: «вечное несчастие» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: He jumped up quickly. “No, this can’t go on!” he said to himself in despair. “I’ll go to her; I’ll ask her; I’ll say for the last time: we are free, and hadn’t we better stay so? Anything’s better than endless misery, disgrace, unfaithfulness!” With despair in his heart and bitter anger against all men, against himself, against her, he went out of the hotel and drove to her house.

cases.explain: «задних комнатах» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: He found her in one of the back rooms. She was sitting on a chest and making some arrangements with her maid, sorting over heaps of dresses of different colors, spread on the backs of chairs and on the floor.

cases.sentence: Она сидела на сундуке и о чем-то распоряжалась с девушкой, разбирая кучи ___, разложенных на спинках стульев и на полу.
cases.explain: «разноцветных платьев» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: He found her in one of the back rooms. She was sitting on a chest and making some arrangements with her maid, sorting over heaps of dresses of different colors, spread on the backs of chairs and on the floor.

cases.sentence: – Ах! – вскрикнула она, увидав его и вся просияв от радости. – Как ты, как же вы (до этого ___ она говорила ему то «ты», то «вы»)?
cases.explain: «последнего дня» — after the preposition «до», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Ah!” she cried, seeing him, and beaming with delight. “Kostya! Konstantin Dmitrievitch!” (These latter days she used these names almost alternately.) “I didn’t expect you! I’m going through my wardrobe to see what’s for whom. …”

cases.sentence: Он уже видел по ее любящему ___, что ничего не может выйти из того, что он намерен был сказать, но ему все-таки нужно было, чтоб она сама разуверила его. – Я приехал сказать, что еще время не ушло.
cases.explain: «правдивому лицу» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “Kitty! I’m in torture. I can’t suffer alone,” he said with despair in his voice, standing before her and looking imploringly into her eyes. He saw already from her loving, truthful face, that nothing could come of what he had meant to say, but yet he wanted her to reassure him herself. “I’ve come to say that there’s still time. This can all be stopped and set right.”

cases.sentence: Его брат, Дарья Александровна и Степан Аркадьич, все в ___, уже ждали его, чтобы благословить образом.
cases.explain: «полном туалете» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Levin, guilty and shamefaced, but pacified, went back to his hotel. His brother, Darya Alexandrovna, and Stepan Arkadyevitch, all in full dress, were waiting for him to bless him with the holy picture. There was no time to lose. Darya Alexandrovna had to drive home again to fetch her curled and pomaded son, who was to carry the holy pictures after the bride. Then a carriage had to be sent for the best man, and another that would take Sergey Ivanovitch away would have to be sent back. … Altogether there were a great many most complicated matters to be considered and arranged. One thing was unmistakable, that there must be no delay, as it was already half-past six.
